steps.title: Prepare polyacrylamide gel solution
steps.instruction: Mix 2.0 ml of 7 % polyacrylamide (bisacrylamide + acrylamide), 3.0 µL TEMED, 2.0 ml distilled water, 4.0 ml of 0.14 % ammonium persulfate, and 0.2 ml Ampholyte High Resolution pH 4–6 (all Sigma‑Aldrich). Allow polymerization to complete.

steps.title: Prepare electrophoresis buffers
steps.instruction: Make cathode buffer containing 0.4 % triethanolamine (TEA) and anode buffer containing 0.2 % sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄), both from Sigma‑Aldrich.

steps.title: Initial electrophoresis to form pH gradient
steps.instruction: Place the polymerized gel in the electrophoretic cell (no samples). Run at 200 V, 1.5 mA for 30 min to establish the pH gradient (use an Incibras power source capable of up to 1000 V).

steps.title: Load samples and run second electrophoresis
steps.instruction: After the 30‑min run, load serum samples (control or patient) into their respective wells; leave selected wells empty for later pH measurement. Run a second electrophoresis at 300 V, 1.5 mA for 210 min.

steps.title: Prepare bromocresol green staining solution
steps.instruction: Combine 59.4 % 0.1 M succinate buffer pH 4.0, 0.95 % Brij‑35 (detergent) 10 %, and 39.65 % bromocresol green 0.6 mM (Sigma‑Aldrich) to obtain a final working solution with pH 4.2 ± 0.5.

steps.title: Stain gel and capture image
steps.instruction: Incubate the electrophoresed gel in the bromocresol green solution for 1 h. After exactly 1 h, remove the gel and immediately capture an image (light exposure thereafter fades the bands).

steps.title: Cut unstained gel pieces for pH measurement
steps.instruction: Cut the portion of the gel that contained no samples into 12 equal pieces, each 0.5 cm long. Place each piece in a glass tube with 2.0 ml distilled water. Store the tubes at 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Measure pH of gel extracts and correlate
steps.instruction: The next day, measure the pH of each tube’s water using a pH meter to define the pH gradient. Compare these pH values with the positions of the stained albumin bands on the gel.
